cap.reading:
The cause is confirmed by the log, the mount-state dump and the code.

1. Ranked 'משחק חדש' runs synchronously in one tick. ResultsScreen.newGame() calls setStarting(true), then onNewGame. In app/results/[id].tsx that runs leave() and then startRankedAndOpen(...,'replace'), which calls router.replace(MATCH_PATH) synchronously (src/screens/home/startGame.ts:73-93). React batches two things into one Fabric commit: Results re-rendering with loading=true, and the replace that creates the /match screen. The dump confirms it: the new RNSScreen 6290 and its SVG views were created in the same failing batch.

2. loading=true changes the native tree of the primary Button. Button.tsx (primary branch, ~line 205) renders `<View style={[styles.content, loading && styles.hidden]}>` around the label. styles.content is only flex layout, so without loading this View is FLATTENED away, and the label Text (5834) is a direct child of the face view (5838). With loading, opacity:0 makes it un-flattenable. Fabric must create View 5836, insert it into 5838 at index 0, and REPARENT Text 5834 into it (Remove 5834 from 5838, then Insert into 5836). The Insert ran while 5834 was still in 5838, so the Remove was not applied first. This commit goes through Reanimated 4.5.1's LayoutAnimationsProxy, which pulls Remove mutations out and rebuilds them (parseRemoveMutations / handleRemovals; Results is the only screen with entering= layout animations, and the action pair sits inside Animated.View entering={enter.actions}). So the reparent's Remove was most likely lost or reordered there. I did not trace which Reanimated branch drops it.
   - The addViewAt throw goes to MountItemDispatcher, then GuardedFrameCallback, then ReactHost.handleHostException.
   - The host is destroyed immediately (getOrCreateDestroyTask at the same ms, not after 10 s). That leaves the window background #0f1218.
   - Tap to exception is about 0.3 s, and the screen goes dark right after.

3. Why this is tonight's regression: in HEAD (87760ce) the same wrapper was `<View style={[styles.content, loading && styles.hidden, { transform: [{ skewX: UNSKEW }] }]}>`. The constant transform kept it un-flattened, so loading never reparented the label. Round 1's Button.tsx rewrite dropped the transform, and that made the wrapper flattenable.

4. The controls fit this cause.
   - Practice 'משחק חדש' works, because startAndOpen is awaited before the replace, so the loading commit lands alone.
   - 'לבית' works, because nothing sets loading.
   - The friends branch (router.replace synchronously after setStarting) is exposed to the same crash. The secondary/danger Button branch has the same flattenable `[styles.content, loading && styles.hidden]` wrapper.

5. Fix candidates. A minimal one is to give the content wrapper `collapsable={false}` (or keep a constant non-flattening prop) in both Button branches, so loading only changes opacity and never reparents. Optionally, also defer the navigation one frame after setStarting(true) (afterFrames), so the loading commit and the replace commit are separate. A regression test should assert that toggling loading does not change the wrapper's presence in the host tree.

6. Separate serious finding (variant a). A ranked game's game-to-Results transition in a process that had already had a K1 host teardown and an in-process relaunch produced a flood of 22,253 Reanimated 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed for tag N' warnings ('RetryableMountingLayerException: Unable to find SurfaceMountingManager'). Each one is logged with a full stack by Log.w on the UI thread, triggered from react-native-svg VirtualView.setClientRect → FabricEventDispatcher → NodesManager.onEventDispatch. Many of the failing tags belong to the dead host's last batch. The UI thread is starved: Skipped 457 and 1107 frames, then an ANR twice (dropbox trace has main in Throwable.printStackTrace ← Log.w ← NativeProxy.synchronouslyUpdateUIProps). Smaller floods (1,975 and 896) also happen in healthy processes on screen transitions (rnscreens ScreenFragment.dispatchTransitionProgressEvent), which matches the 'flood' in docs/PERF.md. Fixing K1 removes the teardown that leads to the extreme case. Still worth a Reanimated patch so it does not log a stack per failure.

fix.rootCause:
The log pins the failing views. In k1-logcat-RF8Y60PP2XZ-3.txt, the mount-state dump (lines 1471-1475) shows the face of the "משחק חדש" button, 5838. Its children are the Slant plate 5830>5828, the label RCTText 5834, and a NEW RCTView 5836. The failing op is "insert 5834 into 5836 at index 0" while 5834 is still in 5838.

5836 is Button.tsx's label wrapper, `<View style={[styles.content, loading && styles.hidden]}>`. styles.content is only flex layout, so Fabric flattens the wrapper and the label sits straight on the face. When `loading` turns on, opacity:0 makes the wrapper un-flattenable. That commit must then create 5836, insert it into the face, and reparent the label (Remove 5834 from 5838, then Insert 5834 into 5836).

On ranked Results, newGame() calls setStarting(true) and then, synchronously, onNewGame. That runs leave() and startRankedAndOpen(...,'replace'), and router.replace('/match') happens in the same tick. So the reparent and the creation of the whole /match screen (RNSScreen 6290 and its SVG views, all parentTag=null in the dump) land in ONE Fabric transaction. That transaction passes through Reanimated 4.5.1's LayoutAnimationsProxy_Legacy (Results has entering= layout animations), which pulls Remove mutations out and re-emits them (parseRemoveMutations/handleRemovals). The label's Remove was not applied before its Insert. The log shows no removeViewAt soft-exception, so the Remove was most likely dropped rather than misindexed. I did not prove which proxy branch drops it.

addViewAt then throws "View already has a parent", and ReactHost.handleHostException destroys the host at the same millisecond, leaving the #0f1218 window background.

This is a regression from round 1's Button rewrite. HEAD 87760ce had a constant `{ transform: [{ skewX: UNSKEW }] }` on the same wrapper, which kept it un-flattened, so loading never reparented the label.

The controls fit this cause:
- Practice awaits startAndOpen before replace, so the loading commit lands alone and the same reparent succeeds.
- 'לבית' never sets loading.
fix.fix:
1) Root fix (apps/mobile/src/components/ui/Button.tsx): in the primary and the secondary/danger branches, the label wrapper is now always its own native view: `collapsable={false}` plus testID `${testID}-content`. The fix has a comment block that explains K1.
   - Toggling `loading` is now only an opacity update on an existing view. No view is created and no view changes parent, so the failing Remove/Insert pair never exists.
   - This covers every Button with `loading` that navigates in the same tick. Besides Results, those are:
     - HomeScreen, GameTypeScreen and BotSelectScreen (`starting`);
     - Login, Register, EditProfile and VerifyEmail;
     - ConfirmModal, among others.
   - The ghost wrapper never changes style, so it was already safe.

2) Isolation for every Results route (apps/mobile/src/screens/results/ResultsScreen.tsx): newGame() sets the spinner, then waits `framesPassed(SWAP_FRAMES)` (the existing retire.ts helper, 2 rAF frames) before onNewGame. So the Results' last commit is mounted alone, before the next screen's commit.
   - This applies to ranked, friends (synchronous router.replace), rooms (dismissTo) and practice/bot alike.
   - A `gone` ref skips the start, and the setStarting(false), if Results unmounts during those frames.

Other routes checked for the same pattern:
- Practice/bot 'משחק חדש' already awaited before replace; it is now also deferred.
- Friends 'משחק חדש' (synchronous replace) had the same exposure and is covered by both changes.
- Levels 'לשלב הבא' uses router.setParams on the same screen, with no Button loading toggle, so it is not affected.
- There is no separate rematch path. "Rematch" is the same Results newGame.
- No other component toggles a style that flattens a wrapper around content. The only other `cond && styles.hidden` is LevelNode's lock and does not happen at navigation.

Old code: there is no such wrapper, so the test fails.

fix.notes:
- No native change, no Reanimated patch, no docs change. The explanation is in a comment in Button.tsx, next to the fix.
- Not proven: the exact LayoutAnimationsProxy_Legacy branch that lost the label's Remove. A stale MutationNode for the face as unflattenedParent would drop it from `roots`; this is a hypothesis only.
  - Both fixes remove the failing condition whatever that branch is: the reparent no longer happens, and the Results update no longer shares a transaction with the new screen.
  - A Reanimated upstream issue or patch could still be worth filing separately.
- Variant (a) is separate and not addressed here: the 22k 'synchronouslyUpdateUIProps failed' Log.w flood leading to ANR after an in-process host relaunch. It should go away with K1, since there is no more teardown, but Reanimated still logs a full stack per failure. A patch-package patch to downgrade that log is a possible follow-up; not done.
- Tests: occasional pre-existing 'An update to AvatarArt ... not wrapped in act' console.error noise in the Results suites. It is not a failure and not from these changes' assertions.
- Diff vs the b3434ea baseline is limited to the 7 files listed.

issues.problem: Nobody has found the Reanimated proxy branch that drops the Remove. The fix removes this one reparent (the Button label), and it splits the Results commit from the navigation commit, but the engine-level condition is still in place. Some other flatten or unflatten reparent that lands in the same transaction as a new screen could still hit it. My read of LayoutAnimationsProxy_Legacy.cpp: a Remove is emitted only if its node is a 'root', meaning nodeForTag_[parent] is not a MutationNode. The practice control (the same Button, the same press, and it works) shows a stale face node cannot be the whole story, so the trigger depends on what the rest of the batch holds.
issues.evidence: Mount dump k1-logcat-RF8Y60PP2XZ-3.txt:1472-1475. 5836 had already been inserted into 5838 when 'insert 5834 into 5836' failed, and 5834 was still in 5838, so the Remove was dropped, not reordered. In node_modules/react-native-reanimated/Common/cpp/reanimated/LayoutAnimations/LayoutAnimationsProxy_Legacy.cpp:234-238, `if (!mutationNode->unflattenedParent->isMutationNode()) roots.push_back(...)`: a non-root Remove is emitted only if its parent goes through startAnimationsRecursively. Both changes avoid this path for the logged sequence. Every `loading={...}` in app/src (27 uses) goes through Button, ConfirmModal or StateView, so the Button fix covers all of them.
issues.suggestion: On the device run, grep logcat for 'addViewAt'/'removeViewAt'/handleHostException across all navigations, not only Results. Consider an upstream Reanimated issue with the mutation trace (LAYOUT_ANIMATIONS_LOGS). No code change is needed for K1.
